item.title: Branch Art Exhibit: Saving the Moment by Jon Christopher Embree — Sun Nov 1, 12:00 AM — Morningside
item.description: Throughout the month of November, the works of Jon Christopher Embree are on display at Morningside branch Jon Christopher Embree showed artistic promise early and started drawing, painting and sculpting from his teens on. With some post-secondary fine arts instruction, he then worked as a graphic artist with a focus on colour theory and retouching. Since retirement he has worked full-time on visual art using oils, pen and ink, watercolour, acrylic as well as sketching, pencil and charcoal. “I want to move people, showcase something that will highlight the beauty of a moment in nature, or the day-to-day environment, ordinary life activities and special places. I want the viewer to stop, breathe slower and think.” This exhibit is part of TPL's Art Exhibit program . Toronto Public Library provides space for local artists to exhibit their work at locations across the city. These exhibits aim to reflect the diverse cultural interests of the city and its neighbourhoods. Free. All are welcom

item.title: Branch Art Exhibit: Dancing Flowers — Mon Nov 2, 12:00 AM — Yorkville
item.description: Throughout the month of November the works of artist Mary Garrone are on display at the Yorkville Branch in an exhibit titled Dancing Flowers. Artist biography: A Toronto-based artist from Australia. She has studied abstract expressionism for two years with the techniques of Nicholas Wilton and Jenny Nelson. A flower photographer for many years, she continues with this subject matter in her acrylic and oil painting. Artist statement: I love the challenge of translating emotion into paintings using gesture, palette, value, shape and line. While each painting is an exhausting number of decisions for me, the artist, the goal is ultimately to bring joy to the viewer. Applying the visual principle that "lines activate," this series is entitled "There's a party in the garden and the flowers are dancing," with each piece conveying an unavoidably positive sensibility with gestures that deliver that message. item.description:

From Yorkville’s beginnings as a nineteenth-century village to the colourful history of Toronto at the time Heliconian Hall came to be, discover the surprising events, eccentric personalities, and forgotten episodes that helped shape Toronto. All are welcome to attend. Doors will open at 6:30pm and the speaker will begin at 7:00pm followed by a Q&A and refreshments. Invite your friends as this is an evening that you won’t want to miss. Categories include pulp fiction, old advertising, concert, travel and movie posters, vintage comics, old photography, postcards, prints, magazines, old paperbacks, out of print books, sports memorabilia, antique maps, unusual, rare and antiquarian books and eccentricities of interest to everyone. item.title: Historical Society of Ottawa - Call to Arms: The Fenian Threat — Wed Nov 11, 7:00 PM — online
item.description:
Guest Speaker Phil Gurski, Author, Historian & former CSIS Analyst Details Among the earliest threats of invasion to stir concern in our new nation’s capital came between 1866 and 1871 as Irish-American militants launched a series of cross-border raids in an attempt to pressure Britain into granting independence to Ireland. Join Phil Gurski as he explores how the Fenian threat exposed vulnerabilities in our young country and helped shape Canada’s early approach to defence, security, and sovereignty. This presentation will take place on Zoom. All are welcome to attend. Registration via Zoom: https://tinyurl.com/HSO-11-Nov-2026
Source: Ontario Historical Society

item.title: The Friends of Fort York and Garrison Common - A "Nation" Divided, A Conversation with Dr. Alan Taylor — Wed Nov 11, 7:00 PM — Yorkminster Park Baptist Church
item.description:
The Friends of Fort York, in partnership with the Canadian Institute for Historical Education, is pleased to host celebrated historian Dr. Alan Taylor. As geopolitical circumstances evolve, we are presented with an opportunity to emphasize the importance of learning more about the long history of relations between Canada and the United States. Join us on November 11, at 7:00 pm, at Cameron Hall at Yorkminster Park Baptist Church (1585 Yonge St.) for a thought-provoking conversation on how we understand national history, how this history influences the moments we remember, or indeed forget, and why it matters on both sides of the Canada-US border. No reservation required, $10 donation encouraged at the door.
Source: Ontario Historical Society

item.title: Oakville Historical Society - Speaker Night "Who Were the Farmerettes?" — Thu Nov 19, 7:30 PM — online
item.description: The Oakville Historical Society is pleased to announce the speaker for our last Speaker Night of 2026, a ZOOM virtual presentation, on Thursday, November 19th, presented by Ms. Bonnie Sitter. During 1941 – 1952, approximately 40 thousand girls between the ages of 16 – 18 went to work on Canadian farms during World War II, to maintain critical food production, the program being sponsored by the Canadian Government. Please join us to learn the story of how the Famerettes were recruited, where they lived, and how they got to camp. See where the camps were established and what their accommodations were like. After tough days in the fields and orchard, learn how they had fun. Hear the stories of these young women, now in their 90s, explain how they still recall what they often describe as the best summer(s) of their lives.
